about.title: Mendota Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Mendota is a small Fresno County farming community, but its roads still see steady traffic where Rt 33 and Rt-180 cross local streets like Oller and Derrick Avenue. Public records show 12 injury collisions and 16 injured people in the most recent final year, with crashes tending to cluster on Sunday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. — likely reflecting weekend travel and agricultural transport patterns in and around town. Whether your crash happened at a rural intersection or on a residential street, the aftermath can be disorienting: medical visits, missed work, vehicle repairs, and calls from an insurance adjuster all at once. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect injured Mendota residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details, explain your options, and handle communication with insurers, all on a contingency basis so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a county road agency — may be involved. Acting early helps preserve your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partially at fault, but your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault. An early, careful review of the evidence helps make sure fault isn't unfairly assigned to you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly after a crash, and anything you say can be used to minimize your claim. An attorney can communicate on your behalf so you're not navigating that alone.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Mendota?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government-owned road or vehicle was involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth getting an early review of your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame — your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. This makes it important to have someone review the police report and evidence before you accept any fault determination.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to another party's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can sometimes hurt your claim. It's generally safer to have an independent attorney handle those conversations for you.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in the LawProactive network, and attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
